stimulus: Welcome to part 1 of our experiment!

Q0: I consent to taking part in this study.

stimulus:
Part I


Task 1

Instructions

In this task, you will see several flowers on a meadow. Your task is to find a hidden bee by clicking on the flowers. After finding the bee, observe its flight from one flower to another, and remember it.

Next, we ask you to redraw the bee's flight path by clicking on one flower and dragging it to another flower. This creates a connection between the two flowers, and a green or red line indicates whether the connection is correct. Only if your redrawing was correct you are led to the next trial, or if you have drawn more than 10 incorrect connections. During this task, the arrangement of the flowers on the meadow may change from time to time, but this should not impede you much.

Note that, firstly, the direction in which you see the bee flying does not matter, because for every direction in which you see a bee flying, we will also present you with the opposite direction. Similarly, it doesn't matter in which direction you draw the connection.

After the task, we will periodically give you a performance score based on your first-attempt accuracy over multiple trials.

Before starting, you can try two example trials by clicking 'Continue.'

You are done with the sample block.


You drew 100% connections correctly on the first try.

Excellent job!

Are you ready?


The testing phase is over. As said before, the task is to remember start and end position of the bee in each trial.

If you are ready you can click on the 'Continue' button, and the experiment begins.

You are done with the first block.


You drew 95% connections correctly on the first try.

Excellent job!

response.strategy: At first, I chose a corner (nw/ne/sw/se) and went by exhaustion. Then I started picking familiar color pairings that were grouped together and started there. Then I decided to start looking for a pattern to predict the location once I noticed that the movements did not seem random. For improvements/suggestions, up until the very first trial, it did not get into my head that I would need to click on the flowers to initialize the bee. I believe I get too focused on the observe a bee movement part of the description. I was expecting the bee to start randomly. This was very simple to learn after the first few seconds and the game play was intuitive , so there was not any difficulty. Nevertheless, it would be helpful to put greater emphasis that the task is to find the bee and track the bee, not  just track the bee.

Task 2

In the following, we show you several pairs of flowers. Please try to remember from the previous task whether the bee knew or did not know the shown flower pair. Again, the directionality is not important in this task.

Indicate your answer with a button click. The task looks like this:

response.strategy: I would like to modify my prior answer. On the question that asks about my confidence in solving the question correctly, at the time of answering, I thought the question was asking about whether I had identified the sequence of pattern so that I could effectively predict any movement based on the prior movement. This is why I marked a low confidence because I had only slightly began to identify the pattern sequences. I am completely confident that I solved the task insofar as shaking the bee and following the bee. For this task, the hardest part was remembering the distinction between gold/orange and yellow pairings. The other colors were sufficiently distinguishable.
